newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian growers see wool market staying strong.
newsitem.headline: Australian growers see wool market staying strong.

text.p: Australian woolgrowers were receiving positive price signals from the wool market, with the Eastern Market Indicator (EMI) ending this week at 753 cents a kg clean, two cents short of the two-year high hit on Wednesday, the Wool Council of Australia said on Thursday.
Fundamentals for the market remained positive for the medium to long term, the woolgrowers' body said in a statement.
Light offerings, renewed interest from China, an end-of-season squeeze and pipeline rebuilding had all contributed to recent strength, it said.
However, the dramatic depreciation of the Australian dollar against Australia's major wool client currencies had probably contributed to the improved run more than any other factor, it said.
Growers should also be examining emerging forward and futures markets, it said.
"Encouragingly, futures volumes have increased dramatically over the past three months and daily volumes have nearly doubled over the past month," the council said.
The recent spike in wool futures had enabled woolgrowers to lock in wool prices which were at premiums to the physical market, it said.
In the short-term the wool market would continue to be largely supply-driven, it said.
Fresh wool may be in short supply following long-range weather forecasts predicting a continuation of dry weather from the El Nino effect, it said.
Added to this was the rapidly reducing Auistralian stockpile, which this week dropped below 1.6 million bales, it said.
Wool International had already completed its stockpiled wool sales commitment for the September quarter and had closed sales in June and July.
"Clearly the stockpile no longer weighs as heavily on the minds of wool processors and the new sales regime is having little impact on the auction price," it said.
